messages:
maria: Heads up — since the 2026-03-15 deploy the Console charts are stuttering on initial load (heatmaps + timeseries). Noticed repeated main-thread jank, CPU spikes and a bunch of re-paints. Anyone seeing this in prod?
jon: Yep reproduced in staging. Opening /metrics causes an initial 400–800ms freeze, then several smaller micro-freezes. Charts mount twice for me.
sophie: I saw that too. My hunch: our prefetch logic triggers a data fetch + render before the chart bundle finishes hydration, causing duplicate mounts. Might be related to recent router prefetch changes.
kevin: Can you paste a short trace or logs? If it's mount churn we should grab a 10s sampling CPU profile from a repro session and a flamegraph. Run locally with: 
```
npm run profile:console -- --url=/metrics --duration=10s
```
jon: Here is a short console log I captured (stripped):
```
[metrics] fetchSeries start 14:12:10.123
Chart.mount start 14:12:10.210
Chart.mount end 14:12:10.300
Chart.mount start 14:12:10.450
Chart.mount end 14:12:10.510
[metrics] fetchSeries end 14:12:10.520
```
maria: That matches what I saw — two mounts before the fetch completes. perf-bot: Artifact diff shows main.bundle.js +120KB and an inlined intl chunk that used to be lazy. Link: https://artifacts.redwood/perf/1865432099
perf-bot: Noted increase in initial bundle parse time ~45ms median.
jon: I think the router prefetch flag is set on the metrics route; webpack prefetch may be pulling the chart chunk earlier, but our prefetch handler also calls a render-intent which triggers a mount. Removing prefetch might reduce double work.
sophie: Also check keys on <Series /> — we had a bug where label objects were mutated so React thought they were new each time, forcing list re-renders. That + prefetch = double penalty.
kevin: Quick experiment: can someone try a canary that disables route prefetch for /metrics and removes the inline intl chunk, then measure charts.mount.count? We should add a telemetry counter for mounts. Suggested metrics: charts.mount.count (increment on mount), charts.first_paint_ms (report first paint after data arrives).
maria: I'll push a tiny canary now: revert prefetch flag + lazy-load intl again. Rolling to 5% to start.
sophie: Also adding a guard in Chart component to ignore mounts if dataRef.current === previousRef (cheap early return).
jon: If the canary looks good, we should add an automated regression test: open /metrics in puppeteer and assert mount_count === 1 within X ms.
kevin: Agreed. Also patch release note: "fix double-mount causing chart stutter" and link to perf dashboard.
deploy-bot: Canary deploy started at 1865432600, traffic=5% (canary-id: c-1865).
maria: Canary metrics are already showing fewer paint spikes in the first 10m — cpu jank down ~60%. Will keep monitoring for 30m.
jon: Nice. If stable after 30m, promote to 100% and add the telemetry counters in a follow-up PR.
sophie: I'll open the PR for the key-fix + guard + telemetry event.
maria: Thanks team — nice triage. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: Canary promoted to 100% at 1865432730 (c-1865).
